cards.body: AI data centers in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, and Indonesia are facing trouble as Nvidia has reportedly ordered its manufacturing partners to stop shipping AI servers to the region. According to the Financial Times, Dell, Supermicro, and other firms that make AI servers using Nvidia AI GPUs have told their customers from the four countries that the AI chip maker has forbidden them to ship their orders. The move comes as the U.S. closed the loophole that let Chinese AI companies rent compute from data centers outside China equipped with advanced AI chips sourced from American semiconductor manufacturers like Nvidia. The U.S. has banned the export of advanced AI chips to China since 2022 in an effort to limit its advancement. Even though President Trump eventually allowed Nvidia to export H100 AI GPUs to China in December 2025, companies that wanted to buy them needed to secure an import license from the Commerce Department. Aside from that, the White House is also collecting a 25% fee for every chip, making it more expensive for a data center in China to buy them. Because of this, many Chinese AI labs are instead renting compute from data centers located abroad. They mostly do this in Southeast Asia, which is just around a four-to-six-hour flight from major cities like Hong Kong, Shenzhen, and Shanghai, although some firms are looking in further areas like Europe . It remains unclear if Nvidia’s order is permanent or temporary, but the new export rules give cloud providers 90 days to apply for an export license and prove that their customers do not include restricted entities. However, one cloud provider executive told the Financial Times that there are no clear instructions on how to go about this. “There’s this new rule but no guidance on execution,” they said. “No one knows how to apply for this license while the 90-day clock is ticking. It’s causing sheer chaos in the region.” This sudden halt of orders is causing trouble for many data centers in Southeast Asia. Sources say that Aolani, a Singapore-based cloud company with a deal to provide compute to ByteDance, is losing financing for the project as bankers have stopped issuing credit to the tune of $500 million as Nvidia GPU shipments to the region remain in jeopardy. The Chinese social media giant could also potentially drop out of the arrangement, as it won’t be able to access the powerful Nvidia chips that many AI labs still prefer for training their models.

cards.body: Nvidia has ordered its manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia in light of the interim final rule issued by the US Department of Commerce earlier this month. According to a report from the FT, companies including Dell and Supermicro have told customers in the affected countries that Nvidia has put a stop to server orders being shipped. It is unclear if the halt is temporary, the report added. Citing Nvidia company accounts, the FT noted that in 2025, the chip giant booked $104 billion in revenue through its Singapore subsidiary – a 72 percent increase over a 12-month period. The company also records some of its revenue from Taiwan and China via its Singaporean operation. The Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry & Security (BIS) issued the new rule on November 16, requiring licenses to export, reexport, or transfer in-country advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil – countries which the government deems to present “a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.” The rule also restricts remote access to advanced AI chips and servers to ensure existing restrictions “cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries.” The rule was issued as a result of the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s admission that he had an affair with a woman who is alleged to be a Chinese spy. Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen) was an executive for Megaspeed, a Singapore-based IT and cloud company currently under investigation for smuggling Nvidia GPUs into China. Earlier this week, the US government added Megaspeed, along with its Thai and Malaysian subsidiaries, to the Commerce Department’s Entity List. Huang resigned on November 12 but was reinstated by the Nvidia board eleven days later, following pressure from President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance. Despite national security concerns that emerged as a result of Huang’s reported behavior, when announcing his return, the Nvidia board of directors said: “In the process of reaching its decision, the board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”

cards.body: Neoclouds are being told they won't be able to purchase Nvidia chips if any of the computing capacity will be rented by Chinese companies, sources told CNBC. It comes after a new rule restricting remote access to artificial-intelligence semiconductors was announced by the Trump administration on Nov. 16. Chip sellers communicated the messaging to neoclouds after the announcement, which seeks to close an export controls loophole allowing Chinese companies to rent access to Nvidia's most advanced chips when hosted in data centers overseas, two people familiar with the situation told CNBC. The people asked not to be named when discussing private information. The interim final rule was announced by the Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, or BIS, and came into effect on Nov. 19. Previously imposed export controls have effectively banned the sale of the most advanced Nvidia chips to Chinese companies and their import into China. Prior to the new rule's announcement, Nvidia had said it would not sell its chips to customers renting more than 50% of the graphics processing units, or GPUs, to Chinese companies, CNBC reported. The new rule impacts the full supply chain, from the companies selling Nvidia chips to the neoclouds who rent access to computing power. Neocloud stocks have come under renewed pressure lately as investors questioned the sustainability of the AI boom. Nvidia and the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Closing 'loopholes' The change has prompted Nvidia chip sellers to look for new buyers of the semiconductor giant's GPUs, CNBC reported on Wednesday, citing three people familiar with the matter. Two of those people said it appeared chip sellers were seeking to offload GPUs because they were originally for use in data centers through which Chinese companies would rent access. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Wednesday that the new BIS rule was intended to close "loopholes." "Some rules were issued by the Commerce Department last week to close off indirect access, either smuggling through places like Southeast Asia or remote access from data centers in third countries," he said. U.S. lawmakers have been looking to clamp down on China's access to advanced compute. Separately, Nvidia warned its customers that the proposed Remote Access Security Act — which has passed the House of Representatives but is yet to pass the Senate — would give the U.S. government broader authority to control access to cloud services, potentially exposing both parties to "legal action," sources previously told CNBC.

cards.body: Sharon AI has installed a fleet of GPUs for Indian cloud provider ESDS Software Solution in Sydney, Australia. As per a regulatory filing by ESDS and reported by w.media, Sharon AI has installed a cluster of 8,208 Nvidia B300s for ESDS, and it is currently undergoing final testing. The cluster is expected to be handed over in mid-December, with customer billing to begin in January 2027. ESDS signed a contract with Sharon AI for the cluster in April 2026. Set to run for five years, Sharon AI said at the time it was a $1.25bn contract. Revenue was previously said to begin in Q3 2026, but ESDS said that the two mutually agreed to revise the schedule and wait for testing before accepting the cluster. ESDS said it will pay Sharon AI approximately $21 million a month for the capacity, and will in turn receive customer payments of approximately $30m, leaving $9m per month in revenue before operating costs and tax. ESDS has already contracted the compute to its customers on a take-or-pay basis. Sharon AI recently published its Q3 2026 earnings results for the period ending September 30, 2026. In its SEC filing, the company noted that it now has $1.68 billion in property and equipment assets, up from just $88.4m in December 2025. This includes $89m in technology equipment, $928,198 in data center equipment, and $1.385bn of "construction in progress." As of September 30, Sharon AI has 129MW of contract capacity across data centers in Australia and New Zealand. This includes a 15MW lease with GreenSquareDC in Australia, capacity in Equinix's SYD3 and SYD5 in Sydney, and 72MW at NextDC's M3 facility in Melbourne. The company also says it has signed a contract for 14MW in New Zealand, but does not share the provider. Revenue for the quarter was $9.93m, up from $506,747 in the same quarter the year prior. However, expenses were significant, with the company seeing a $37.46m loss from operations in the quarter, compared to $1.5m the year prior. The quarterly report noted that Sharon AI is in "an investment phase and is incurring material earnings losses, and its cash outflows in respect of investing activities continued to exceed cash inflows from operating activities ... During the third quarter of 2026, the Company accelerated the deployment of next-generation GPU clusters under long-term customer arrangements, resulting in substantial cash requirements ahead of expected revenue generation." The company has a remaining performance obligation of $3.8bn, with 35 percent expected to be realized within 24 months and all of it within 6.5 years. The neocloud listed on the Nasdaq stock exchange in February 2026 with a $125m IPO. According to that filing, the company had just 432 GPUs and 195 CPUs online across its footprint in Australia, as of September 2025. During the Q3 earnings call, CEO James Manning said that a 1,000-GPU cluster was accepted by a customer in August, and 30MW of capacity will be billed from January 2027. cards.body: The fact that high-end Nvidia AI cards reach China despite the U.S. export controls isn't so much an open secret as it is simply a pricing structure. Several write-ups have illustrated that fact in the past, but today's Washington Post chronicle details how easy it is to buy the forbidden goods in China right now, with no need for secrecy or private club passwords — just talk to the sellers who have them. The Post details how one of its correspondents went to the Huaqiangbei market in the Shenzhen prefecture — a location known for its variety of technological goods — to try and get some export-controlled Nvidia Blackwell cards. Seemingly at the cost of only a bit of conversation, an initially reluctant seller named Wu made a few calls and eventually quoted around $3 million for an eight-GPU server with Blackwell B300 chips, the highest-end version. Equivalent hardware purportedly sells for around $500,000-600,000 in the U.S., but it apparently sells easily even with the apparent 5-6x markup. Plenty of Chinese companies are producing their own wares, yes, but at this point in time, no chip family comes close to the massive horsepower offered by Blackwell. This is a parallel story to U.S. firms, who are happy to overpay for server hardware even when the contracts they've signed change underneath them. While inference tasks (running the models) can be performed as well or, arguably better, with efficiency-oriented alternatives, training a frontier-level model requires astounding amounts of compute power, to the tune of thousands of B300s. Hence, according to Kyle Chan from the Brookings Institution, Nvidia's wares are a 'decisive factor' in the performance-starved Chinese AI market. A Shenzhen-based consultant put it plainly, saying that if he ever wanted to have an AI firm, he'd just go to Huaqiangbei and "work out a deal." Proving that point, the publication found more sellers dealing in Blackwell rack units, with price tags of $3-3.4 million for an eight-GPU machine. According to seller Jason Cheng, his clients include folks from Russia and Iran, nations also covered by the U.S. AI trade export controls. The fact that those people opt to just fly to China and pay a sizable markup instead of trying to procure the GPUs more directly themselves may illustrate how well-oiled China's grey-market supply chain is. Wu told the Post he gets his cards from Hong Kong, though he's apparently unaware of where they hail from in the first place. The Post raises questions about how the trade controls are taking effect, highlighting Washington's inconsistent stance on the matter, with the Treasury and the Department of Commerce seemingly at odds regarding enforcement. Heck, even procurement records for Chinese public institutions reportedly show clear purchase orders for forbidden wares. Whither Nvidia in all of this? The other one, which is on Nvidia's list of "preferred partners," is owned by a Chinese firm whose CEO graduated from a Chinese military university. It's reported that U.S.-based, Chinese-owned companies have been used as a way to work around export controls designed to prevent Nvidia's chips from being sold wholesale to China. Chips are routinely sold to companies in the U.S. before being leased or shipped to other companies in Southeast Asia. While Nvidia isn't allowed to sell its most capable AI chips to China, it can still do business with the country. It can sell graphics cards for use in personal gaming PCs as well as AI chips that don't use the company's latest, most capable technologies. But that hasn't stopped those chips from turning up in the most unlikely of places. Illegal Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs have been spotted in use inside China Telecom's network , and last year alone, it's believed that around $1 billion worth of Nvidia chips were smuggled into China. Earlier this year, nine people were indicted over the illegal export of Nvidia GPUs , while even older Nvidia hardware has seen huge price increases due to the unavailability of newer hardware. Megaspeed is one company that is accused of facilitating the breaking of export controls. The company is under criminal investigation currently , and it was recently blacklisted as a result . The company also happens to be a former employer of Alice Huang, the woman whom Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to having an affair with when he resigned from the company earlier this month. stage1.korean_title: 엔비디아, 데이터센터 냉각 스타트업 Madrone에 50만 달러 투자

headlines.body: A startup promising to cut data center cooling bills with a novel chiller-free system has raised $500,000 from backers including Nvidia. Madrone, which is part of the Y Combinator business incubator program, has raised the cash in a seed round backed by the GPU giant, as well as Y Combinator itself and investment firm Tekedia Capital. Founded by Akshay Trikha and Erik Meike, Madrone says its modular system will sit outside the data center and supply cool facility water that can be used in servers. It claims it will do this using a thermodynamic process, without the need for the kind of mechanical chillers often found in data center cooling setups. Precisely how it intends to do this has not been revealed by the company, but it is trumpeting some big potential savings. With up to 30 percent of data center power being dedicated to cooling, Madrone’s thesis is that, by using its system, this power could be redirected to serve the data center’s hardware, giving operators a potential $78 million in additional revenue per 100MW of GPUs per year. It should be noted that many data centers already choose to eschew mechanical chillers in favor of free cooling, using the ambient air to reduce the temperature of cooling fluid, but this is not practical in hot environments, which is where Madrone is hoping to clean up. The company cites the example of Texas, the second largest data center market in the US, as an area where its system could work particularly well. Meike has some cooling experience, having previously worked as a thermal engineer at Apple, while Trikha deployed machine learning systems at battery technology firm QuantumScape. The pair have built a 100kW demonstrator unit, but will need to scale up their technology significantly to enable it to be deployed at data center scale.

She had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who abruptly resigned on Nov. 12 after acknowledging it and was just as abruptly reinstated on Monday of this week. What’s publicly known is murkier than the headlines suggest. U.S. intelligence has reportedly tracked Alice Huang’s contact with an officer of China’s spy agency, but officials haven’t offered public evidence that she was commissioned to target Nvidia’s chief. In the past week, after President Trump successfully pushed to bring Jensen Huang back, the administration has played down the allegations it once circulated internally. Whether that reflects new intelligence or political pressure is the big question. Undisputed reporting shows the claim emerged from the White House itself. It first appeared in a highly classified memo written in March under the oversight of Secretary of State Marco Rubio and circulated to White House officials ahead of Trump’s trip to China in May. The memo formed the partial basis for the New York Times’ initial reporting on the scandal, published Oct. 29 and its existence was first reported on Nov. 8. The memo did not definitively say, according to the Wall Street Journal, that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy. CNN, by contrast, has reported that the memo concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset. What’s better established is that Alice Huang was in touch with Chinese intelligence. The Ministry of State Security (MSS) is Beijing’s civilian spy agency, responsible for both foreign intelligence and domestic counterintelligence. Last weekend, the Times, citing people with knowledge of U.S. intelligence reports, reported that Huang was in contact with an MSS officer from the spring of 2025 until this fall, a period that overlaps her relationship with Jensen Huang. headlines.title: Credit rating agency puts Nvidia on notice for possible downgrade

stage1.korean_title: S&P, NVIDIA 신용등급 강등 경고
stage1.korean_summary: 신용평가사 S&P가 Jensen Huang 의혹 및 경영진 감시 약화를 이유로 신용등급 강등 가능성 경고.

headlines.body: S&P Global Ratings, one of the world’s largest rating agencies, announced that it’s putting Nvidia’s credit rating on watch as the company faces a possible downgrade. The agency says that the issues surrounding Jensen Huang regarding export control violations, as well as his resignation and subsequent reinstatement 11 days later, reveal the weakness of Nvidia’s management team and board oversight. “We believe the long tenure of certain board members may have compromised their independence,” the rating agency said in its press release. It also added, “Issues related to Nvidia’s China exposure also raise questions regarding geopolitical risk management and internal controls. While Nvidia management has delivered significant returns for its stakeholders over decades, weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning have brought questions around the ‘key man’ risk to the forefront. The departure, then reinstatement of the CEO, does not sufficiently answer our questions regarding board oversight of executive code of conduct.” Nvidia CEO and founder Jensen Huang resigned from the job on November 12, after multiple allegations of affairs, especially with Megaspeed CEO Alice Huang, who’s also accused of enabling the smuggling of $7.5 billion worth of AI GPUs into China. Even though Huang left the company he founded in disgrace , he was reinstated to the position by the Nvidia board on November 23. This was a major surprise, especially as it had previously refused to bring him back due to the ongoing national security investigation into Jensen. However, it seems that Nvidia’s board of directors has folded to the pressure, especially after President Donald Trump himself said that he talked to them directly , with the board saying that it “received input from senior levels of the United States” that “Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” Despite those assurances, the Nvidia chief still faces multiple investigations , including an internal inquiry at Nvidia, a private meeting with the House of Representatives’ Select Committee on China, and a public testimony in front of the Senate Banking Committee, among others. Even though the AI chipmaker’s risk profile remains unchanged, S&P Global Ratings’ warning is a sign that the market is uneasy about the situation regarding stricter export controls and the allegations of chip diversion. The ratings agency said that the downgrade could happen in the next 90 days after it concludes its due diligence, although it expects any potential drop to “be limited to one notch, unless investigations or disclosures lead us to believe Nvidia’s reputation or future business prospects have been harmed.”

headlines.title: US defense officials considered using Cold War law to force Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO following his resignation, report claims

stage1.korean_title: 미 국방부, Defense Production Act로 Huang 복직 강제 검토
stage1.korean_summary: 미국 국방부 고위 관리들이 냉전시대 법 DPA를 활용해 Jensen Huang CEO 복직 강제 가능성 검토.

headlines.body: Following the resignation of Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO after admitting to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, U.S. defense leaders considered invoking a Cold War-era law in an attempt to force the company to reinstate him, according to a new report. Huang was given his CEO job back earlier this week, with the board reminding the founder of the importance of "candor and honesty" in the future. Now, The Washington Post reports that U.S. officials were so keen to ensure that Huang was reinstated that they brainstormed ideas as to how they could make it happen. One of the options on the table was the Defense Production Act, or DFA, a 1950 law that allows presidents to interfere with private companies. The law is usually used to force those companies to supply the military during wartime, but Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and his senior deputy, Steve Feinberg, wondered whether it could also be used to put pressure on Nvidia's board. While the DFA doesn't explicitly give the president the power to place a particular person into the CEO role at a company, it could still be wielded to achieve the same result. “Essentially, they could use the DPA to force Nvidia to shift more of its production to military projects,” one of three people reportedly familiar with the discussions said. Such a move would have limited Nvidia's ability to sell components for a profit, affecting its production plans and share price as a result. The way in which U.S. officials pushed for Huang's return before his November 23 reinstatement is unprecedented. Current U.S. President Donald Trump called for Huang to be given his job back on multiple occasions, including when talking to reporters at the White House . Trump also confirmed that he called into an Nvidia board meeting to pressure members to bring Huang back just 11 days after he resigned. And with Huang still set to face questions from China congressional and Senate Banking committees , Trump has admitted that a pardon for the CEO is "always an option." This came after it was suggested that Huang could plead the Fifth Amendment for fear of incriminating himself and landing himself in legal hot water. The U.S. military views Nvidia and its advanced AI chips as vital to national security, perhaps explaining why officials have been so keen to ensure Huang's return. Trump and Huang have a strong relationship, with the former joining the president aboard Air Force One for a recent trip to China. This came after Huang was initially snubbed for a trip that also included former Apple CEO Tim Cook and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.

headlines.body: U.S. President Donald Trump says that he could pardon returning Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang if he finds himself in legal hot water over his already-admitted affair with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed employee and an alleged Chinese spy . The Nvidia founder has since admitted to the company's board that he had more affairs than those already reported , including one with a direct report . Huang is set to meet with the House Foreign Affairs Committee next week and will be expected to answer questions about the affair, its effect on Nvidia, and how it impacts the national security of the country as a whole. Trump pushed for Huang's reinstatement, going so far as to pressure the Nvidia board via a telephone call. With that in mind, a NY Post report that he could consider pardoning Huang may not be all that surprising. Discussing Huang's meeting on December 1, Trump argued that the two-time Nvidia CEO doesn't need to worry about pleading the Fifth Amendment to avoid incriminating himself. Instead, Trump says, the whole saga is "an interesting story for people,” suggesting that perhaps the American people will learn more in the future. “I think I want him to just tell the truth, and I mean, his lawyers are going to have to advise him, but I’ve always found him to be 100% aboveboard, and you know, a very smart person,” Trump said of the man whose mistress is also married to an alleged Chinese spy herself. U.S. intelligence officials believe that Alice Huang passed information about Nvidia to Chinese officials during her affair with Jensen Huang (no relation). The good news, it seems, is that Trump is of the understanding that Alice Huang is the only woman Jensen was having an affair with who also has links to China's Ministry of State Security. When pushed on the potential for a pardon for Huang if he was found to have broken any laws, Trump admitted that “It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary.” The news will no doubt be music to the ears of Huang, with lawmakers expected to give him a grilling and some already not expecting him to be forthcoming in terms of the answers he offers to their questions. Nvidia's top lawyer will also have to answer questions about the company's position in all of this, although that'll come a day later, on December 2.

headlines.body: 끝없이 긍정적일 것만 같던 인공지능(AI) 시대의 미래에 대한 믿음이 기로에 섰다. AI 기술의 발전 가능성에는 의심의 여지가 없지만, 산업의 지속적인 성장과 수익성에 대해서는 의구심이 커지고 있다. 주식시장에서는 이미 ‘AI 거품’에 대한 위기감이 제기됐고, 최근 몇 달간 AI 관련주가 큰 폭의 조정을 받으면서 이러한 우려가 상당 부분 현실화됐다. AI 시대의 록스타로 꼽히는 젠슨 황 엔비디아 CEO의 복귀에도 시장의 불안감은 완전히 해소되지 않았다. AI의 잠재력은 모두가 인정한다. 하지만 관건은 ‘비용’이다. 지금까지 AI는 미래 가치를 보고 투자하는 영역이었다. 투자자들은 당장 수익을 내지 못하더라도 사용자가 늘고 수익성이 개선될 때까지 기다릴 수 있다는 자세였다. 실제 AI 이용량은 크게 늘고 있다. 매달 사용되는 토큰 수는 2년 전보다 300배 이상 늘었다. 만년 적자에 머물 것 같던 거대 AI 기업들도 이제 손익분기점에 근접해 가고 있다. 하지만 AI에는 여전히 비용 문제가 남아 있다. 1년 가까이 이어져 온 AI발 메모리 대란은 인프라 구축 비용을 크게 높였고, 이는 AI 서비스 운영 전반에 부담으로 작용하고 있다. 새로운 데이터센터에 최신 그래픽처리장치(GPU)가 설치되면서 토큰당 처리 비용은 줄었지만 최신 에이전틱 AI 모델이 하나의 작업을 수행하는 데 사용하는 토큰 수가 폭증하면서 오히려 ‘작업당 비용’은 늘었다. 글로벌 하이퍼스케일러들은 대규모 인프라 투자로 현금 여력이 줄어든 상황에서도 추가 투자 자금을 확보해야 하는 상황에 놓였다. AI 산업의 다음 병목 지점이 기술에서 ‘자본’으로 옮겨갔다는 평가가 나오는 이유다. 하드웨어 인프라 비용이 불과 1년 전보다 크게 오른 상황에서 투자금 회수를 고민해야 하는 기업들의 입장에서 보면 AI는 아직 갈 길이 멀다. 기술의 발전과 확산이라는 측면에서 분명한 성과를 거뒀지만, 비용 절감과 수익성 개선은 몇 년 전의 기대에 미치지 못하고 있다. 기술이 발전할수록 비용이 줄어든다는 기존의 성공 방정식과는 오히려 반대의 흐름이 나타나고 있다. 지금까지는 기술 확산과 사용자 확보를 위해 발생하는 손실을 투자금으로 충당했지만, 수익성을 증명하지 않고 이러한 구조를 유지할 수 있는 시간은 얼마 남지 않았다. 기술이 보편화되기 위해서는 기술적 완성도뿐만 아니라 소비자들이 기꺼이 비용을 지불할 수 있는 가격 합리성이 중요하다. 기술이 일정 수준의 완성도에 이르면 결국은 가격이 승부를 가른다. 아직 AI는 이 단계에 이르지 못했다. AI 업계의 경쟁적 인프라 투자가 촉발한 반도체 공급난과 가격 상승은 이 길을 더 멀고 험하게 만들었다. 앞으로의 AI 시대의 성장을 이끌 핵심 경쟁력은 프론티어 모델의 성능 못지않게 ‘비용’이 될 것이다. 이미 업계 전반이 이런 방향으로 움직이고 있다. 최근 구글과 마이크로소프트가 성능을 유지하면서 추론 비용을 크게 낮춘 모델들을 선보였다. 하드웨어에서도 GPU에 대한 의존도를 낮추고 자체 설계한 AI 전용 가속기의 활용을 늘리고 있다. 오픈AI와 앤트로픽 등 프론티어 모델 개발사들도 성능 향상과 함께 추론 비용 절감과 서비스 가격 경쟁력 확보에 힘을 쏟고 있다. 이러한 추세는 AI 인프라 시장의 ‘GPU 만능론’도 바꿀 것이다. 범용성과 연산 효율 사이에서 균형을 추구한 GPU는 기술과 모델의 변화가 빠른 시기에는 유연함이 강점이다. 하지만 AI 모델과 서비스의 유형이 일정 수준 정형화되면 특정 연산에 최적화된 전용 가속기가 비용과 전력 효율 측면에서 더 높은 경쟁력을 확보할 수 있다. 이 시기가 오면 현재 AI 인프라 시장의 선두인 엔비디아도 지금과 같은 독보적 지위를 유지하기 어려울 수 있다. 많은 기업이 이 시기를 노리고 있다. 엔비디아 또한 이러한 변화에 대비하고 있겠지만, 아직 뚜렷한 성과가 나온 것은 아니다. 최근 젠슨 황 엔비디아 CEO가 논란 끝에 복귀했다. 그의 사임과 복귀를 전후해 글로벌 주식시장은 큰 변동을 겪었지만, 이것이 단지 업계의 리더를 잃어서 그렇다고 해석할 수는 없다. AI 시대의 미래 고민은 록스타 한 명이 돌아왔다고 끝날 일이 아니다. AI를 얼마나 합리적인 비용으로 구현하고 지속 가능한 수익으로 연결할 수 있는지를 고민해야 할 때다. 권용만 기자 yongman.kwon@chosunbiz.com

headlines.body: BEIJING — The household robot could soon become a reality, Brian Gu, co-president of Xpeng, a Chinese electric car company which has entered the humanoids space, told CNBC. "Maybe after successful deployment into commercial settings, maybe another one to two years, we can start thinking about deploying into home settings," Gu said. "Technology is moving at a much faster clip." Xpeng revealed its latest general-purpose humanoid robot Iron on Wednesday. The company plans to start training the robot as a store assistant in its retail car locations in the first quarter next year, after starting mass production in January. Sales are set to begin in the second quarter, with deliveries expected later in the year. Founded in 2014 as an electric car company, Xpeng beat Tesla to rolling out driver-assist in mainland China. The Chinese automaker has launched its own artificial intelligence chips. It's also expanded into personal flying vehicles and robotics. The robotics unit this summer raised $900 million at a $6.3 billion valuation in its first funding round, led by IDG Capital. Investors, however, appear to be a tad skeptical about the developments at Xpeng, with the downturn in the Chinese auto market also weighing on the company. Xpeng's shares, listed in both New York and Hong Kong, have dropped more than 55% this year amid broad sector declines. China's humanoid industry has faced more regulatory scrutiny on financing in recent months after Unitree's high-profile IPO and stock slump, as well as a rush of capital into the sector. That's all raised questions about commercialization and the efficacy of the core tech. Gu said Xpeng's robotics stands out for its rare combination of the hardware, software and real-life use cases. He's expecting to add more investors after Iron's planned commercial launch next year. "You can always make the head talk, you can always make the leg run, you can always make the hands to do certain tasks," Gu said. "But doing a task while you're walking and answering questions at the same time, that's the most challenging part. And then doing everything well, not falling down, not getting distracted. The model has to work in sync." Most humanoid robot startups, especially in China, focus on a portion of the tech, such as hands or the artificial intelligence-powered brain. headlines.body: 엠앤앤에이치(대표이사 민병왕)가 광운대 서영호 교수 연구팀과 함께 생성형 AI 비디오와 월드모델, 피지컬 AI의 영상 데이터 수요에 대응하는 H.266 VVC Encoder IP를 개발했다. 비트리는 이 IP를 자사 피지컬 AI 영상 통합 플랫폼 'WALNUT'의 VPU 포트폴리오에 적용할 계획이다. 개발팀은 고객의 반도체 설계 조건에 맞춰 처리 성능·압축 효율·로직 크기를 조절하는 유연한 설계를 적용했다. 영상을 만드는 AI 기술과 이를 전송·저장하는 압축 기술을 연결하고, 서로 다른 공정과 시스템 요구에 대응하는 영상 반도체 설계자산(IP)을 마련했다. 생성형 AI의 발전은 영상을 만드는 방식뿐 아니라 전달하고 보관해야 할 데이터의 규모도 바꾸고 있다. 구글의 Project Genie는 사용자의 행동에 따라 가상세계를 실시간으로 생성·편집한다. 이런 클라우드 서비스에서는 사용자마다 다른 장면을 계속 전달해야 하므로, 하나의 영상을 반복 재생하는 서비스보다 전송 데이터 관리가 중요해진다. NVIDIA Cosmos는 로봇·자율주행 개발에 필요한 가상환경과 합성 영상을 생성한다. 다양한 상황을 재현할수록 활용할 영상이 늘어나고, 이를 보관하고 개발 과정에서 공유하는 부담도 커진다. 즉, AI가 만들어내는 영상의 가치가 실제 서비스와 개발 현장으로 이어지려면, 필요한 화질을 유지하면서 전송·저장 데이터량을 줄이는 기술이 뒷받침돼야 한다. VVC는 이 전송·저장 구간의 데이터량을 줄이는 국제 영상 압축 표준이다. 프라운호퍼 HHI는 다양한 영상과 응용에서 VVC가 H.265/HEVC 대비 같은 주관적 화질을 유지하면서 비트레이트를 약 50% 줄인다고 설명한다. 이는 표준 기술의 압축 잠재력으로, 필요한 화질을 유지하며 압축 데이터량을 줄이면 같은 네트워크·저장 자원으로 더 많은 영상을 다룰 여지가 생긴다. 압축 효율을 실제 칩의 경쟁력으로 바꾸는 데에는 VVC의 복잡도가 장벽이다. 정교한 블록 분할과 예측·변환 도구는 연산과 메모리 접근 부담을 늘릴 수 있다. 압축 도구를 확대하면 효율을 높일 여지가 있지만 로직 규모가 커질 수 있고, 병렬 처리를 늘리면 처리량과 함께 면적·메모리 요구도 증가할 수 있다. 적용 공정의 특성과 동작 주파수, 칩 면적, 전력, 압축 효율 사이의 균형이 필요한 이유다. VVC 소프트웨어 구현인 VVenC도 품질·속도 프리셋과 세부 설정을 제공한다. 하드웨어 IP에서는 이 선택을 칩의 자원 구성에 반영하는 설계 역량이 중요하다. 엠앤앤에이치는 압축 도구의 선택·최적화와 코어 병렬화 구성을 조합해 이러한 상충관계에 대응했다. 고정된 최고 사양을 모든 제품에 넣는 대신, 칩 설계 단계에서 고객이 필요한 성능·압축 효율·로직 크기의 조합을 선택하는 구조를 적용했다. 면적·원가 제약이 큰 제품에는 압축 도구 구성을 최적화하고, 고해상도·고프레임률 제품에는 병렬 연산을 확대하며, 전송·저장 비용이 중요한 제품에는 VVC의 모든 기능이 구현되어 압축 효율 중심의 구성을 선택할 수 있게 했다. 공정과 시스템 자원에 맞춰 설계 지점을 조정하는 유연성을 제품의 핵심 차별점으로 구현했다. 이러한 설계는 소형 엣지 카메라와 로봇·차량용 영상 시스템부터 고해상도 생성형 영상 처리까지 적용 범위를 넓히는 기반이 됐다. 전용 하드웨어 압축 경로를 구성하는 VVC IP와 고객 맞춤형 설계를 결합해, AI 연산과 영상 압축이 함께 필요한 시스템의 자원 배분에 대응했다. 성능·압축 효율·면적을 무조건 동시에 개선한다는 뜻이 아니라, 시장별 요구와 칩의 제약에 맞는 균형점을 선택하도록 한 것이다. 개별 구성의 효과는 적용 공정과 영상 조건에 따라 달라진다. 이번 VVC Encoder IP는 한국반도체협회 시스템반도체 설계지원센터에서 지원하는 '2026년도 반도체 IP 상용화지원 프로그램 2차'의 지원을 받아 산·학 3개 기관이 공동으로 개발했다. 엠앤앤에이치가 VVC IP 전체 개발을 총괄했고, 광운대학교 서영호 교수 연구실은 VVC 설계 최적화와 핵심 블록 개발을 담당했다. 비트리(각자대표 김희걸·김종필)는 ISP와 VVC 압축 출력을 연계하는 통합 최적화를 맡았다. 이미지 센서 출력을 영상으로 만드는 ISP 단계와 이를 압축하는 단계 사이에서 생기는 불필요한 메모리 접근과 데이터 이동을 줄이는 것이 목표다. WALNUT 적용 과정에서는 비트리의 실시간 스트림 기반 영상처리 기술을 접목해 피지컬 AI에 필요한 실시간 영상 처리와 영상 기록·전송을 함께 지원한다는 계획이며, 양사는 이를 패키지 IP 형태로 사업화하는 방안도 추진하고 있다. 이번 개발은 기업과 대학의 기술 협력을 바탕으로 IP 개발부터 플랫폼 통합·사업화까지 연계하는 기반을 마련했다는 데 의미가 있다. IP 에 대한 자세한 사양과 공정은 국내 반도체 IP 관리 플랫폼인 IP360 에서 확인할 수 있다. 이원지 기자 news21g@etnews.com - 이원지 기자기사 더보기 - ET Events

README:  # Nemotron-3.5-Rerank-8B-BF16 Overview ## Description: **Nemotron-3.5-Rerank-8B-BF16** was developed by NVIDIA for multilingual and multimodal question-answering retrieval. It is a world-class reranker optimized to produce a logit representing the relevance of a document to a text query. Documents may contain text, page images, or both, including charts, tables, and infographics. The model can be integrated into classical or agentic vision RAG pipelines. For text retrieval, the model was evaluated across 34 languages: English, Arabic, Assamese, Bengali, Bulgarian, Chinese, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, French, German, Hindi, Hinglish, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Malay, Marathi, Nepali, Norwegian, Persian, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Spanish, Swahili, Swedish, Tamil, Telugu, Thai, Ukrainian, Urdu, and Vietnamese. For image retrieval, it was evaluated across 18 languages: Arabic, Bengali, Chinese, English, Persian, Finnish, French, German, Hindi, Indonesian, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Spanish, Swahili, Telugu, Thai, and Yoruba. The model may support additional languages beyond these evaluation sets. Nemotron-3.5-Rerank-8B-BF16 achieves state-of-the-art results on the new [ViDoRe v3.1 Reranking leaderboard](https://leaderboard.mteb.org/benchmark/ViDoRe(v3.1)) as of October 20, 2026. Read more details in our [Blog Post](https://huggingface.co/blog/nvidia/nemotron-retriever-world-class-agentic-retrieval). This model is ready for commercial or non-commercial use. ### Licen
